name: Rum Village
tagline: The gateway settlement and visitor center
description: The main settlement inside the reserve, home to the Wadi Rum visitor center where you pay entry and meet guides. A small Bedouin village with basic shops, a few cafes, and the strongest mobile signal in the area. It is the practical hub rather than a scenic base.
bestFor: First arrival, buying supplies, and meeting your camp
pros: Best mobile signal in the reserve
Basic shops and cafes for supplies
cons: Not scenic compared to the deep desert
Limited amenities and no real nightlife

name: Central Valley Camps
tagline: Classic desert camps among the massifs
description: The iconic camp zone spread across the central valleys beyond Rum village, tucked beneath towering sandstone and granite massifs. Home to traditional tented camps and the famous bubble domes, this is where most visitors sleep, dine on zarb, and stargaze. Reached only with Bedouin drivers.
bestFor: The core desert experience and stargazing
pros: Authentic camp dinners and tours on the doorstep
cons: Weak or no wifi and patchy signal
Basic facilities and remote from services

name: Diseh (Disi) Area
tagline: Camps on the northern edge of the desert
description: The Disi and Diseh area on the northern fringe of Wadi Rum, with its own cluster of desert camps and easier road access from the highway. Slightly less dramatic than the central valleys but convenient, quieter, and often a touch cheaper, with the same red sands and rock formations nearby.
bestFor: Easier access and calmer, value camps
pros: Simpler road access from the highway
cons: Less iconic than the central valley

name: Aqaba (Gateway)
tagline: Red Sea road base into Wadi Rum
description: Not part of the reserve but the closest real town, about an hour away on the Red Sea coast. Aqaba has hotels, restaurants, an airport, reliable wifi, and diving, making it the logical place to work, resupply, and sleep before or after a desert stay in Wadi Rum.
vibe: Relaxed coastal town and logistics hub
bestFor: Reliable wifi, resupply, and travel connections
pros: Restaurants, hotels, and Red Sea diving
cons: An hour from the desert itself
